title: MRPO: Magnitude-Regularized Policy Optimization via L1 Constraints
claim: A familiar regularizer concentrates mass on top-reward actions and suppresses low-probability ones; our alternative gives them larger boosts and leaves marginal ones untouched.
layout: 2 side-by-side bar-chart panels, shared axes, overlaid reward line with star markers
description: Two side-by-side toy histograms. Each plots probability π(a) over a ranked set of discrete actions on the x-axis. Hatched gray bars show the reference policy π_ref, which is skewed toward a few actions. A dark-red line with star markers shows reward decreasing across actions. The left panel overlays the KL-optimal policy π*_KL in navy hatching. It sharply amplifies a few top actions and shrinks the low-probability tail. The right panel overlays the L1-optimal policy π*_L1 in teal hatching. It shifts mass more broadly toward high-reward actions, and the actions with marginal changes match the reference. Legends with math labels sit at the lower right of each panel. The eye goes first to the tall bar in the left panel and then compares it with the right panel. The right panel is cropped at its right edge.

abstract: Reinforcement learning (RL) for large language models (LLMs) relies on imperfect reward supervision, necessitating constraints on policy updates to prevent overfitting. Nevertheless, the widely adopted KL constraint over-penalizes actions with low reference probabilities and lacks the sparsity to discard marginal policy shifts. In contrast, the L1-norm offers a distinct mechanism that is more tolerant of low-probability actions yet strictly suppresses minor probability perturbations. Motivated by this, we propose Magnitude-Regularized Policy Optimization (MRPO), which enforces an L1-norm constraint on policy updates. We demonstrate that MRPO permits substantial probability boosts for low-probability actions and induces sparse updates, ensuring invariance to noise that preserves the top-ranking order. Furthermore, MRPO admits a TRPO-style monotonic improvement bound under standard regularity assumptions and achieves a tighter approach to optimality than KL-based methods in single-step scenarios. Empirically, MRPO delivers exceptional results across diverse scenarios, notably doubling the performance gains of GRPO in preference alignment, outperforming DAPO in mathematical reasoning, and surpassing DPO in offline settings using only binary rewards.
